title: Field diary: quant eval weekly (Oct 06 2027)
content:
Purpose
- Quick capture from this week’s scrappy research standups. Focus: small-batch quant experiments, a couple of surprising eval regressions, and checklist progress for onboarding a 13B raft-style model. Meant to be informal — notes, hypotheses, and who’s doing what next.

Highlights / TL;DR
- 4-bit PTQ with folding (experiment QPT4-F) saved ~3.6x memory and ~1.9x peak-power on local RTX8000 but caused a 2.8% drop on our in-house accuracy suite for instruction-following prompts.
- QAT warm-start attempt (seed from float fp16 + 2 epochs) recovered ~1.6% of the lost accuracy but increased training time by ~2.3x vs light PTQ tweaks. Still worth exploring for high-value model families.
- Unexpected: small context-length-dependent hallucinations when KV-cache merge heuristics run with 4-bit keys. Repro steps noted below.
- Onboarding checklist for raft-13b: tokenization mismatch found (byte fallback behavior) — patched tokenizer loader in repo PR referenced.

Weekly standup notes (2027-10-06)
Attendees: Aisha (lead capture), Kai, Evan, Sofia, Rakesh (infra drop-in)
- Kai: running microbatch sweep across 8 vs 64 batch sizes for QPT4-F; saw throughput cliff at batch size 16 for sequence length >1024. Suspect kernel memory fragmentation.
- Evan: eval harness flagged an out-of-distribution failure on the redwood_inhouse_promptset for few-shot math style questions. Failure correlates with single-token repetition in beam search when logits rescaling applied.
- Sofia: onboarding checklist at 65% complete — tokenizer bug + config mismatch fixed (see PR). Waiting on model artifact hashes from infra.
- Rakesh: infra validated multi-GPU sharded loading for raft-13b but runtime mem limit still at 92% for 4-bit + prefetched KV cache. Recommends temporary mem-squeeze flag in runner.

Experiment runs and quick metrics (raw capture)
- QPT4-F (PTQ w/ folding, symmetric per-channel, no per-tensor clipping)
  - baseline float fp16 perplexity (redwood dev eval): 13.2
  - QPT4-F perplexity: 14.0 (+6%), redwood_inhouse_acc delta: -2.8%
  - mem footprint: 3.6x improvement over fp16 checkpoint on local node
  - median token latency: +12% (kernel overhead for dequant path)

- QAT-light (warm-start):
  - init from fp16, 2 local epochs with dropout 0.0, learning-rate 2e-5
  - recovered accuracy: +1.6% vs QPT4-F (still -1.2% vs fp16)
  - training time: ~2.3x of PTQ flow (experiment resource expensive)
  - qualitative: fewer short-answer hallucinations, better numeric stability for arithmetic prompts

- KV-cache merge regression (repro):
  Steps: load raft-13b QPT4-F, feed prompt A (multi-sentence context, ~1200 tokens), generate with kv_prefetch=on and kv_merge_heuristic=adaptive -> observe repeated non-deterministic factual hallucination in slot 2 at generation step 87.
  - Disabled kv_prefetch in runner -> problem disappears.
  - Hypothesis: 4-bit key quantization + prefetch reorders cache load and triggers stale KV reads due to alignment rounding. Open ticket JIRA-ML-1284.

Model onboarding snapshot (raft-13b)
- Checklist progress: artifact ingestion (done), tokenizer runbook (patched), config linting (pending), model card draft (in review), eval suite baseline (running).
- Tokenizer issue: fallback bytes-mode caused OOV spikes on Italian datasets — fixed in tokenizer-loader PR (see linked artifact). Please re-run tokenizer testset before gating onboarding.
- Storage: staging artifact uploaded to s3://redwood-staging/raft-13b/digest-v3 but hash mismatch reported on infra side. Evan to re-upload with streaming checksum.

Open questions and hypotheses to test next
1) Is the KV merge regression unique to our folding strategy or generic to any aggressive per-channel 4-bit quant? Run same prompt with an alternative 4-bit scheme (asymmetric per-tensor) and compare. (Owner: Kai)
2) Can we adopt a hybrid approach: 8-bit keys + 4-bit weights to avoid KV corruption while preserving memory wins? Quick microbench to compare mem vs accuracy. (Owner: Sofia)
3) For high-sensitivity evals (math/facts), does QAT with only final-layer fine-tune recover more than 2 epochs of whole-network QAT? Cheaper to run than full QAT. (Owner: Evan)

Action items (short)
- Kai: run alternative 4-bit scheme on same prompt set (deadline: 2027-10-12).
- Evan: re-upload raft-13b artifact with streaming checksum + post here when done (deadline: 2027-10-07).
- Sofia: microbench hybrid (8-bit keys + 4-bit weights) — collect perf, mem, and accuracy numbers (deadline: 2027-10-11).
- Aisha: add succinct summary to the quant-playbook confluence page and paste this diary; add link to JIRA-ML-1284 (deadline: 2027-10-08).

Notes to self
- Remember: when reporting accuracy deltas, show both absolute and relative to the in-house instruction-tuned baseline. People care more about nuance for product gating.
- Keep a short reproducibility snippet for each experiment: command line, model hash, seed, sequence length. Makes later triage much easier.

Appendix: quick reproducibility snippets (for later copy/paste)
- Run QPT4-F reproduce: tools/quant/bin/ptq_run --model s3://redwood-staging/raft-13b/digest-v3 --scheme perchannel-symmetric --folding true --seed 42 --seq-len 2048 --batch 8
- KV regression repro: python infra/run_gen.py --model local/raft-13b-qpt4f --prompt-file experiments/kv_regress/prompts/a.jsonl --kv-prefetch true --kv-merge adaptive --seed 1234

End of capture.

(laid out rough, will tidy and move final notes into confluence once we have the re-uploaded artifact and the kernel debug from infra)
